annotation.title_clean: Advisory Guidelines on Use of Personal Data in Generative AI
annotation.title_en: Advisory Guidelines on Use of Personal Data in Generative AI
named_instruments_referenced: PDPC Advisory Guidelines on Use of Personal Data in AI Recommendation and Decision Systems
PDPC Advisory Guidelines on Key Concepts in the PDPA
annotation.summary_en: Singapore PDPC advisory guidelines explaining how the PDPA applies to generative AI across development, deployment and post-deployment. They cover the publicly available exception for web-scraping, consent and notification, roles of model providers, system providers and deployers, and access and correction requests. Non-binding; no robotics content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Organisations may rely on the Publicly Available Exception to web-scrape personal data, subject to a reasonable-person test; digital barriers require assessment.
Consent and AI-specific notification are needed for using user data in model development; consent cannot be a condition of service beyond what is reasonable.
Organisations are encouraged to anonymise and minimise data and apply technical and legal protection controls.
Responsibilities are allocated among model providers, system providers and deployers.
Access and correction requests should be handled case by case, with data provenance records and output filters as safeguards.
